Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards â€” an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command ships with a <fowler-pass-record-path> placeholder; record() runs that command and refuses `pass` while it fails. NORMAL PATH -- resolve the placeholder to the real record path when you INSTANTIATE this survey from the template, before you claim: it is an instantiation-time substitution exactly like <work-id> on line 2. That is the documented route and the one you should be on. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record later moves or the path you substituted was wrong, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

c2-nonvacuous.title: CC2: the test is not vacuous
c2-nonvacuous.imperative: Attack the new test for vacuity: does it assert the REFUSAL (not merely no-crash); is the gauge reading live inside the assertion window; would it still pass if the fixture never reached active_id != gate-being-closed? Probe by perturbing the fixture in a scratch copy. Record pass/fail with a finding.
c2-nonvacuous.finding: Not vacuous, attacked six ways with an independent probe (.agent-work/.../g3-rework-review/antivacuity_probe.py, imports the shipped engine + the test module's own helpers, touches nothing). P2: in the fixture's state at fill=0.12 the two readings the mutation chooses between genuinely DIFFER -- _trip_hard_band_reading(cl,'.','g2') returns a Reading (require_why) while _trip_hard_band_reading(cl,'.') returns None. That is the discriminator, live. P3 (the decisive counterfactual): the SAME fixture WITHOUT the block leaves active_id==g2, both readings return a Reading, and advance is refused under shipped AND under the mutant -- so a no-divergence fixture would kill nothing; the block step is load-bearing, and the test does not merely rely on it, it ASSERTS it (assertEqual(E.active_id(cl),'g1')), which converts future silent vacuity (e.g. if block() ever gains a status guard) into a red test rather than a quiet pass. P4: the gauge reading is live inside the assertion window -- identical fixture and verb closes cleanly at fill=0.00 ('g2 -> complete') and refuses at 0.12 and 0.99. P5: the refusal is specifically the no-silent-close rule ('cannot be closed silently'), and the same close WITH --why SUCCEEDS -- so the assertion is about the silence, not about a gate that cannot close at all. P6: the same public-verb sequence with NO override on g2 CLOSES at the same 12% fill, so the refusal is attributable to the override, not to the blocked-g1 shape. The test asserts the refusal itself (assertRaises + assertIn 'cannot be closed silently' + g2 still 'in-progress'), not merely that nothing crashed. NB-1 (non-blocking): the test carries no in-test positive control of the P5/P6 kind; the mutation kill and the explicit active_id assertion carry that load instead.

c3-public-verbs.title: CC3: divergent state reached through PUBLIC verbs
c3-public-verbs.imperative: Confirm the fixture reaches active_id != gate-being-closed through public engine verbs (start/advance/start/block/advance) and not by hand-mutating checklist JSON into an engine-unreachable shape. Record pass/fail with a finding.
c3-public-verbs.finding: Reached through public verbs only, confirmed by re-driving the sequence myself (probe P1): gated() builds an ordinary two-gate checklist, then dispatch start g1 / advance g1 / start g2 / block g1 -- every step through E.dispatch, the same CLI boundary the engine exposes; the block call is a types.SimpleNamespace matching _run_verb's block branch (id/blocker/authority/next_action), which is what argparse produces, not a hand-shaped dict. The only direct JSON write is cl['tasks']['g2']['context_headroom_tokens']=50000, which is the authored override this issue ships and is exactly how the pre-existing tests in this class declare it -- not a status or ordering forced by hand. Resulting statuses {'g1':'blocked','g2':'in-progress'} with active_id=='g1' are produced by the engine, not written. So the kill is not hollow: the state the original EQUIVALENT declaration called an 'unreachable fixture' is reachable, and the manufactured-fixture defence it rested on does not apply.
